title: Lemon-Pepper Pork Cutlets with Skillet Gravy
description: Thin pork cutlets poach in broth and finish under a lemon-pepper gravy made with a pale butter roux.

ingredients.name: boneless center-cut pork loin chops
ingredients.note: Trim fat and slice horizontally into cutlets about 1/3 inch thick.

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.note: Choose plain meat-and-bone broth without a vegetable blend.

steps.title: Warm the poaching broth
steps.text: Heat {broth} to a gentle simmer in the HexClad over medium heat.

steps.title: Poach the cutlets
steps.text: Set {pork} in the broth in one layer and cover. Simmer on low for 4–8 minutes, turning once. Check each center from the side and lift each cutlet when it reaches 145°F.

steps.title: Rest in the juices
steps.text: Rest the pork in a covered bowl with a little hot broth for at least 3 minutes.

steps.title: Reserve the broth
steps.text: Pour the remaining poaching broth into a heatproof jug for the gravy.

steps.title: Make a pale roux
steps.text: Melt {butter} over medium-low in the empty HexClad. Whisk in {flour} and cook for 1 minute, stirring continuously.

steps.title: Thicken the gravy
steps.text: Whisk the reserved poaching broth slowly into the roux. Bring to a boil and simmer 2–3 minutes until the gravy coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Serve in gravy
steps.text: Slice the rested pork against the grain, slide it into the gravy and spoon the remaining gravy over the top.

notes: Make ahead: Slice the pork a day ahead and refrigerate it covered. Make the roux while the cooked cutlets rest. Option A includes lemon and pepper. For gentler Option B, omit both the juice and zest and leave the pepper for the table. For dairy-free gravy use avocado oil instead of butter. Refrigerate promptly in shallow portions and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze the cutlets in gravy for up to 2 months. Whisk the gravy as it warms to restore the texture. Fridge reheat: Warm a single portion with its sauce in a covered HexClad skillet over medium-low, adding a splash of water if thick. Stir or turn gently and begin checking after 5 minutes. Heat the food to 165°F throughout. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator. Use the fridge reheating directions and stir the sauce smooth. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/2 of recipe): 245 kcal, 35.2 g protein, 3.4 g total carbohydrate, 10.2 g fat, 0.2 g fiber, 142 mg sodium. Includes the measured broth and sauce. Sodium varies with your broth.

steps.text: Start the enamel Dutch oven over medium-low heat for 2–3 minutes; use the lid for covered steps. Reduce heat once liquids simmer and stir across the heavy base.
